Key Takeaways

Credo Technology fell 14% today as an AI hardware sell-off over Democrats' midterm sweep entered a second day.

The drop prices in a slower data center buildout that hasn't shown up in Credo's guidance or analysts' estimates.

Oracle, Arista Networks and Bloom Energy fell too, though Oracle and Arista still report fast-growing AI demand.

Credo's forward P/E is at a three-year low, and its December report is the next test.

Credo Technology (CRDO:NASDAQ) stock is down 14% today, the day after it fell 10% on Democrats' midterm sweep.

The selling hit AI's builders and suppliers. Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) is down 6%, Arista Networks (ANET:NYSE) is off 9%, and Bloom Energy (BE:NYSE) is down 15%.

A Texas-sized worry

In Texas, Gina Hinojosa beat Gov. Greg Abbott on a promise of an immediate data center moratorium, and Yorkville Ives & Co.'s Dan Ives says 25% to 30% of coming data center capacity will come from the state. Wells Fargo's chief equity strategist, Ohsung Kwon, had warned that a Democratic win in that race could be a "left-tail event" for the AI trade.

Credo feels that more than most: its active electrical cables supplied over 99% of its revenue growth in fiscal 2026.

Bloom fell even after NTT DATA announced a 900 MW fuel cell agreement with it this morning. Investors are selling the theme.

Credo's outlook hasn't budged

In September, Credo guided fiscal second-quarter revenue to $525 million-$535 million and full-year growth of more than 85%. Analysts expect revenue to nearly triple from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028:

Credo Technology (CRDO): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2022-2028 (years to April) (TIKR)

A slower Texas buildout would hit the fiscal 2028 estimate first; this year's has management's guide behind it.

The spending behind those numbers hasn't slowed yet. Oracle delivered 850 MW of additional data center capacity in its quarter ended Aug. 31 and said in September that AI cloud demand is still growing faster than supply. Arista guided on Tuesday for fourth-quarter revenue of $3.9 billion-$4.0 billion, up from $3.66 billion in the third quarter.

TIKR tracks 20 analysts on Credo Technology. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Credo Technology, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Credo Technology's Analyst Ratings

Cheaper than it's been in years

Credo's forward P/E sat at 19x on TIKR's latest reading, a three-year low and far below its 63x average:

Credo Technology (CRDO): forward (NTM) P/E, last 3 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's even lower.

The risk is concentration: four customers bought 84% of Credo's revenue in the quarter ended Aug. 1.

Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) shares sank 9.3% to $112.22 at 10:55 a.m. ET on November 5 during regular trading. The enterprise software and cloud provider's AI expansion has put a tougher question in front of investors: how much capital will it take to turn massive commitments into cash? The session decline sharpened the focus on funding needs and the pace of infrastructure delivery.

Oracle's September 10 earnings release reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $19.3 billion, with cloud infrastructure revenue jumping 121% to $7.4 billionapproximately 38% of the total. Remaining performance obligations reached $664 billion. Oracle also completed $20 billion in common-equity sales during the quarter to support its capital investment program. The demand figures are substantial, but contracted business still needs capacity before it can become recognized revenue.

The GuruFocus snapshot gives Oracle a GF Score of 89/100, with profitability and growth standing out while financial strength and momentum trail those stronger readings. It also flags four severe warning signs, adding a caution alongside the strong overall score. For investors, the next test is execution: how quickly Oracle brings capacity online, converts commitments into cash and manages further funding needs. Selling equity supplies capital, but it also spreads future earnings across more shares. Strong demand could support the expansion; delivery and cash generation will determine whether the spending pays off.

Why Oracle stock is falling after Democrats' midterm sweep

Two days after Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, investors are selling anything tied to AI data centers. They're concerned that tighter political scrutiny will slow the build-out.

A moratorium on data center development was a key part of many Democratic campaigns, especially in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio, each of which just elected a Democrat as governor.

Texas alone accounts for about a quarter of the U.S. compute capacity due online by 2030 and is a key state in Oracle's AI build-out.

Image source: Getty Images.

How Oracle's debt raises the stakes in the AI build-out

Oracle has more or less bet-the-farm on the AI trade, taking on significant debt in order to fund its massive data center projects. As of August, the company had about $125 billion of debt, and much more off balance sheet.

A major slowdown -- frankly, even a slight delay -- could seriously endanger the company's prospects.

Snowflake SNOW shares have gained 32.5% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 9% gain and the Zacks Internet Software industry's 3.5% decline.

The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, including major players like Oracle ORCL, Broadcom AVGO and Amazon AMZN, which are also expanding their footprint in the AI space. While Oracle and AVGO shares have plunged 36.5% and 6%, respectively, Amazon shares have gained 15.2% year to date.

The outperformance can be attributed to SNOW's strong AI adoption and increasing usage of its platform, as reflected by the net revenue retention rate of 126% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. These factors are helping SNOW fend off competitors like Oracle, Broadcom and Amazon.

SNOW Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

SNOW Benefits From Expanding AI Portfolio

Snowflake is benefiting from an expanding AI portfolio. The company has rapidly broadened its suite of AI-powered products, including CoCo and CoWork, which are seeing strong adoption across a diverse customer base. The company launched more than 330 generally available product capabilities during the first half, including Cortex Sense and Cortex AI Gateway, strengthening its ability to offer governed AI, model choice and agentic workflows.

Building on this momentum, the company recently introduced major enhancements to its CoCo coding agent and CoWork personal AI agent, enabling enterprises to automate complex workflows using governed business data. The new always-on CoCo and CoWork Bots autonomously execute tasks, requiring human intervention only for critical decisions or approvals.

The innovations support integrations with Slack, Excel, Google Sheets and mobile devices, while introducing automation, memory and shared AI workflows. Snowflake also unveiled Cortex Training for customizing AI models and optimizing costs. CoWork is used by more than 5,800 accounts, while CoCo serves more than 9,100 accounts.

Further expanding its enterprise AI portfolio, Snowflake introduced new AI capabilities designed to help enterprises deploy autonomous agents with trusted business context, enhanced security, and centralized governance. The new Business Ontology feature within Snowflake Horizon Catalog enables AI agents to access consistent, pre-approved business definitions, improving accuracy and reliability. The company also expanded Cortex AI Gateway to provide unified controls for agent activities, model access, security, compliance and spending. Additional capabilities include Cortex Sandboxes, Agent Abuse Detection and Dynamic Model Routing. Enterprises including Glean and Kargo are leveraging Cortex AI Gateway, while dentsu and Merkle are adopting Business Ontology to strengthen AI-driven operations.

Strong AI demand is improving Snowflake's financial outlook. For fiscal 2027, the company raised product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, implying 36% year-over-year growth compared with the previous outlook of $5.84 billion and 31% growth. Fiscal third-quarter product revenues are expected to be between $1.588 billion and $1.593 billion, indicating 37-38% growth.
